English: Reed Mat
Simple mats of woven reeds, laid on bare ground, serve as sleeping pads and workspaces for the first arrivals.
Woven Shelter
Temporary shelters of woven reeds and branches shield families from the elements and foster clan unity.
Wattle Hut
Wattle and daub huts offer sturdier shelter, allowing for modest stores and the beginnings of a stable camp.
Thatched Pavilion
Large, communal pavilions with thatched roofs serve as gathering points for the clan, fostering unity and managing supplies.
Mudbrick Room
The first semi-permanent mudbrick structures provide shelter from harsh weather and enable year-round occupation.
Fenced Yard
Wooden palisades define the clans space, protecting livestock and supplies, and allowing for efficient organization.
Family Hall
A large wooden hall at the center hosts feasts, clan councils, and strengthens the bonds within the tribe.
Village Chamber
Multiple halls and chambers support the bustling life of a permanent Magyar settlement, boosting population and unity.
Chiefs Pavilion
A grand, bedecked pavilion houses the chief and his retinue, symbolizing Magyar leadership and inspiring the clan.
Magyar Grand Hall
A vast, majestic hall of wood, earth, and stone, seat of the Magyar khan and heart of the nation, radiating unity and strength.
